canonicalName: Group theory from the solution of polynomial equations

evidence.claim: Liouville printed Galois' memoirs in his journal in 1846; group-based solvability theory outlined there
Galois' term 'groupe de l'equation' appears in the memoir written 1830, first printed 1846
evidence.source: MacTutor, Earliest Known Uses of Some Words of Mathematics (G)

evidence.claim: Lagrange's 1770 work on equations is where permutations of roots were first studied
evidence.source: MacTutor, History topic: The development of group theory

conceptual.note: Dated to the first printed statement of a group of permutations of roots as an object (Galois, written 1830-32, printed 1846). Precursors: Lagrange's Reflexions (presented 1770; print year of the Berlin Nouveaux Memoires volume not verified), Ruffini 1799 book (MacTutor Ruffini), Cauchy's 1815 permutation memoir (MacTutor Cauchy). If the event's idea is read as the abstract group, the date would be Cayley 1854 (see institutional).

evidence.claim: Galois' printed memoirs give a group-theoretic criterion for solvability by radicals

methodological.note: First purposeful use of the permutation group on the target problem (solvability). Later systematic use: Jordan's papers 1865-1870 and the 1870 Traite (MacTutor Jordan). No bibliographic record of the 1846 journal issue was retrieved (archive.org search for the 1846 Journal de mathematiques gave 0 hits).

evidence.claim: Cayley's paper 'On the theory of groups, as depending on the symbolic equation theta^n = 1', Phil. Mag. 1854
Cayley's 1854 papers define an abstract group with a multiplication table
Jordan, Traite des substitutions et des equations algebriques, 1870
Burnside's 1897 Theory of Groups of Finite Order: first group-theory treatise in English

institutional.note: Earliest paper title naming the field found: Cayley 1854 (Crossref). First monograph: Jordan 1870 (archive.org). Netto, Substitutionentheorie und ihre Anwendung auf die Algebra, 1882 (zbMATH JFM 14.0090.01; Open Library). Serret's Cours d'algebre superieure (1849, 1854, 1866 editions on archive.org) taught substitutions earlier but its title does not name the field. Searched zbMATH titles 'Gruppentheorie' 1868-1895 and 'theory of groups' 1868-1885; JFM coverage starts 1868.

works.citation: Galois, E., Oeuvres mathematiques (J. Math. Pures Appl. 11, 1846); later edition with E. Picard
works.whyItMatters: Contains the memoir introducing the group of an equation and the solvability criterion

works.citation: Cayley, A., On the theory of groups, as depending on the symbolic equation theta^n = 1, Phil. Mag. 7 (1854)
works.whyItMatters: First abstract definition of a group, detached from permutations of roots

works.citation: Jordan, C., Traite des substitutions et des equations algebriques, Paris 1870
works.whyItMatters: First monograph organising permutation-group theory around Galois' ideas

works.citation: Dyck, W., Gruppentheoretische Studien, Math. Ann. 20 (1882)
works.whyItMatters: Groups given by generators and relations, a step toward groups independent of permutations

works.citation: Burnside, W., Theory of Groups of Finite Order, Cambridge 1897
works.whyItMatters: First group-theory treatise in English

notes: Three plausible conceptual anchors: Lagrange 1770 (permutations as tool), Galois printed 1846 (group as object), Cayley 1854 (abstract definition). Galois' work was written 1830-32 and announced by Liouville in 1843 (MacTutor), but printed only in 1846. Axiomatisation independent of permutations continues with Dyck and Weber (1882) and the American postulate papers 1902-1905 (cited in the MacTutor topic bibliography); not separately verified here. Lagrange and Ruffini omitted from people because no bibliographic record of their works was retrieved.

evidence.claim: Szele, Kombinatorische Untersuchungen ueber den gerichteten vollstaendigen Graphen, Mat. Fiz. Lapok 1943
Alon and Spencer call Szele's tournament result the first proof by the probabilistic method

conceptual.note: Szele's thesis was completed 1941 but the paper appeared 1943 (MacTutor). Attribution of 'first' rests on Alon-Spencer as reported by MacTutor.

evidence.claim: Erdos, Some remarks on the theory of graphs, Bull. AMS 53 (1947) 292-294

methodological.note: The 1947 note is the standard example of a deliberate counting/random-colouring argument for Ramsey lower bounds; the record verifies the paper, the method attribution follows standard histories (e.g. Alon 2013 chapter 'Paul Erdos and Probabilistic Reasoning', doi 10.1007/978-3-642-39286-3_1) and was not checked against the text.

evidence.claim: Erdos and Spencer, Probabilistic Methods in Combinatorics (book), 1974
Alon and Spencer, The Probabilistic Method, Wiley 1992 (later editions 2000, 2008, 2016)

institutional.note: First monograph naming the field. Later: Spencer, Ten Lectures on the Probabilistic Method (CBMS 1987, zbMATH 0703.05046); Spencer ICM 1994 address 'Probabilistic methods in combinatorics' (Crossref 10.1007/978-3-0348-9078-6_132). zbMATH title search 'probabilistic method' 1900-1985 shows earlier uses only in other fields (radiative transfer, 1960s).

canonicalName: Non-Euclidean geometry: the independence of the parallel postulate

evidence.claim: Lobachevsky's account, the first in print, appeared in 1829 in the Kazan Messenger
Lobachevsky published a work on non-Euclidean geometry in 1829; Saccheri and Lambert earlier denied the postulate

conceptual.note: Kazan Messenger serial 1829-30. Bolyai's Appendix to his father's Tentamen followed (conventionally 1832; MacTutor says written up after 1831, exact print year not verified here). Gauss's views were private correspondence only (MacTutor Gauss). Precursors: Saccheri 1733, Lambert's Theorie der Parallellinien written 1766 (MacTutor Lambert).

evidence.claim: Beltrami's 1868 'Saggio di interpretazione della geometria non-euclidea' gave his famous model
Beltrami, Teoria fondamentale degli spazii di curvatura costante, Annali di Mat. 1868
French translation 'Essai d'interpretation de la geometrie non-euclidienne', Ann. ENS 1869

methodological.note: Purposeful use on the target (consistency, hence independence of the parallel postulate relative to Euclidean geometry) via surfaces of constant negative curvature. Klein 1871 gave the projective model (Crossref 10.1007/bf02100583).

evidence.claim: Lobachevsky, 'Geometrie imaginaire', J. reine angew. Math. 17 (1837) 295-320

Halsted's 1878 'Bibliography of hyper-space and non-Euclidean geometry' (archive.org jstor-2369314) marks bibliographic consolidation.
